skill.name: playwright-testing
skill.description: Provides Playwright E2E testing guidance for configuration, locators, fixtures, page objects, debugging, accessibility checks, and network mocking.
skill.summary: Helps build, debug, and maintain Playwright end-to-end tests.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives caused by Markdown examples, localhost Playwright configuration, and CI flag usage. One medium risk remains: the community skill includes an executable Bash setup checker, so it should be reviewed and run only with explicit user approval.

remediation.issue: Executable setup helper in a community skill
remediation.suggestion: Keep scripts/check-playwright-setup.sh opt-in, document the commands it runs, and require user confirmation before execution.

remediation.issue: Project-local tooling may run through the setup checker
remediation.suggestion: Avoid automatic npx execution from skill instructions. Ask users to approve any command after reviewing project dependencies.

content.value_statement: Playwright suites can become flaky when configuration, locators, and fixtures are inconsistent. This skill gives practical patterns for reliable browser tests, debugging, and reusable page objects.
actual_capabilities: Explains Playwright configuration for browsers, reporters, web servers, retries, and CI behavior.
Guides locator selection, page object design, fixtures, and auto-waiting assertions.
Shows network mocking, API error handling, request interception, and header modification examples.
Covers accessibility checks, visual regression tests, screenshots, traces, and debug modes.
Includes a page object template and a local setup checker for Playwright projects.
limitations: It does not run tests unless the user or agent invokes Playwright commands.
Examples use generic login and form flows that must be adapted to each application.
The setup checker targets Node projects with package.json and Playwright configuration files.
It does not replace project-specific test architecture review.

use_cases.title: Configure Playwright Projects
use_cases.description: Set up browsers, reporters, retries, web servers, traces, and CI-friendly defaults for an E2E suite.

use_cases.title: Refactor Test Structure
use_cases.description: Move repeated browser actions into page objects, fixtures, and clearer test flows.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Flaky Tests
use_cases.description: Replace fragile waits, improve locators, inspect traces, and add failure screenshots.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Test File
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one Playwright test.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Playwright test file for locator quality, waits, assertions, and obvious flake risks. Suggest small, safe improvements first.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Playwright configuration for CI reliability, browser projects, reporters, traces, screenshots, retries, and webServer settings.

prompt_templates.title: Design Page Objects
prompt_templates.prompt: Help design page objects and fixtures for this feature area. Keep responsibilities clear and avoid hiding important assertions.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Flaky Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these failing Playwright tests for flake causes. Prioritize locator problems, async timing, test isolation, network dependencies, and CI differences.

output_examples.input: I need better locators for checkout tests.
output: Prioritizes role and label locators for visible controls.
Suggests scoped locators for repeated rows and cards.
Flags brittle CSS selectors that depend on layout or generated classes.

output_examples.input: My Playwright suite fails only in CI.
output: Checks retry, worker, trace, screenshot, and web server settings.
Looks for missing browser installation or unavailable environment services.
Recommends targeted waits based on user-visible state.

output_examples.input: I want reusable page objects for login and dashboard tests.
output: Separates navigation, actions, and assertions into clear responsibilities.
Keeps locators close to the page object that owns them.
Suggests fixtures only where they reduce repeated setup.

best_practices: Prefer user-visible locators such as roles, labels, headings, and accessible names.
Use traces, screenshots, and videos on failure before adding broad retries.
Review community Bash helpers before running them in a project workspace.
anti_patterns: Relying on fixed sleeps instead of waiting for visible application state.
Hiding important assertions inside page objects where test intent becomes unclear.
Running setup or install commands automatically without user confirmation.

faq.question: Does this skill run Playwright tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Tests run only when a user or agent executes Playwright commands.

faq.question: Can it help with flaky tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on locators, auto-waiting assertions, test isolation, traces, and CI-specific configuration.

faq.question: Does it support page object patterns?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes page object guidance and a reusable TypeScript template.

faq.question: Can it help configure CI runs?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers retries, workers, web server reuse, traces, screenshots, and browser project configuration.

faq.question: Does it include accessibility testing guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples using accessibility checks with Playwright-compatible tooling.

faq.question: Should I run the included setup checker?
faq.answer: Review it first. It is a local Bash helper that inspects a Node Playwright project.
